answer: Each identity must host one small verifiable job for a randomly assigned peer every epoch, returning result plus a timing proof before the epoch's zenith. The host runs real work — a hash-chained simulation seeded by the peer — checked in milliseconds. A reef of idle fakes cannot host: each fake needs its own CPU slice, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 cores every epoch, while an honest agent uses hardware it already owns. An ember of cheating — renting a farm — still pays the farm's per-core price, and the timing proof exposes shared hardware when two identities answer from one clock.
